routes.label: Use a median and base-height area
A horizontal base through the midpoint

question: Circles with centers \(P,\) \(Q\) and \(R,\) having radii \(1,\) \(2\) and \(3,\) respectively, lie on the same side of line \(l\) and are tangent to \(l\) at \(P',\) \(Q'\) and \(R',\) respectively, with \(Q'\) between \(P'\) and \(R'.\) The circle with center \(Q\) is externally tangent to each of the other two circles. What is the area of \(\triangle PQR?\)
solution:
Tangency gives both the center distances and the heights above \(l\). Orient \(l\) horizontally with \(P',Q',R'\) in that order from left to right. A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to \(l\), so the centers have heights \(1,2,3\), respectively. External tangency also gives
\[
PQ=1+2=3,\qquad QR=2+3=5.
\]
The vertical difference is \(1\) for each pair. The Pythagorean theorem therefore gives the horizontal separations
\[
u=P'Q'=\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=2\sqrt2,
\]
\[
v=Q'R'=\sqrt{5^2-1^2}=2\sqrt6.
\]
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(PR\). By the midpoint theorem, its height above \(l\) is \((1+3)/2=2\), the same as \(Q\), and its horizontal position is halfway between \(P'\) and \(R'\). Thus \(QM\parallel l\). Since \(v>u\), the point \(M\) is to the right of \(Q\), and
\[
QM=\frac{u+v}{2}-u
=\frac{v-u}{2}
=\sqrt6-\sqrt2.
\]
Segment \(QM\) divides \(\triangle PQR\) into \(\triangle PQM\) and \(\triangle RQM\). Using their common horizontal base \(QM\), each has height \(1\). Hence
\[
[ PQR ]
=\frac12 QM\cdot1+\frac12 QM\cdot1
=\boxed{\sqrt6-\sqrt2},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
